subject: Sizing & commitment proposal: fleet allocation options for ZenHealth regulated workloads
thread_content:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zenhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05 14:07:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Redwood sizing questions for isolated inference

Thanks Aditya — attaching a short metrics dump. We're evaluating two flavors: (A) Hosted Dedicated in Redwood (single-tenant but cloud-managed) and (B) Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for the regulated imaging / PHI workflow. Key asks: 24/7 availability, <120ms median latency on 512-token prompts for our reporting model, ability to drive bursts up to 250 qps for a five-minute window, and SOC2-compliant audit trails.

Attached: zenhealth_workload_metrics.csv (sample qps/seq length distribution)

Can your team sketch what a deal-linked fleet commitment would look like (GPU counts, headroom for bursts, recommended quantization/model variants) and an ROI/commitment horizon? Procurement wants a delta between Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) vs Private (initial infra + maintenance) ideally in a single slide.

--
Alex Kim
IT Architect, ZenHealth

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Redwood sizing questions for isolated inference

FW: ZenHealth metrics. They want a compact, deal-linked sizing comparison (dedicated reserved vs private infra) with explicit GPU counts, burst headroom, and a suggested commitment term. I started a couple of back-of-envelope calcs below — please iterate and produce a short proposal we can send to Alex + Procurement.

Quick context: target model is a 13B customer-reporting model (dense), baseline 512 tokens, target P50 latency <120ms. From metrics: 60% requests <= 256 tokens, 35% ~512 tokens, rare >1024. Typical observed steady QPS ~40; they need baseline 24/7 with spikes up to 250 qps for 3–5 minutes (daily batch/ingest).

My initial thinking (very rough):
- Dedicated (cloud-managed reserved): aim for an H100-equivalent pool sized to sustain steady 40 qps at P50 <120ms and allow autoscale bursts to 250 qps using burst instances and model-variant fallbacks. Rough: 8 H100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state, + dynamic pool of 6 burst GPUs. Commitment: 36-month reserved gives best unit economics.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): you'd want stronger headroom for overhead and redundancy: 12 H100-equivalent GPUs (N+1 for maintenance), robust network and caching layer; higher 1x capex but lower per-token cloud margin after 24–36 months.

Can you provide more defensible CPU/GPU counts, cost delta given a 24-month and 36-month horizon, and an ops/responsibility table (who manages upgrades/security/audit logs)? Also add a short recommendation (sales angle) for the procurement ask: staged commitment: start Dedicated with a 12-mo reserved + private pilot 3–6 months, or go straight Private if legal requires air-gap.

Thanks — Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-06 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: RE: FW: Redwood sizing questions for isolated inference

Aditya / team — I ran the metrics through our workload model and patched in conservative kernel/kv-cache behavior. Key assumptions: 13B dense model; batch scheduling with 32-token average micro-batch for GPU utilization; quantized P8 available (gives ~1.6x throughput improvement with minor ans loss) and a model-variant fallback for critical SLAs.

Summary (defensible numbers):
- Steady state: 40 qps at P50 <120ms -> 6 x H100-eq GPUs (with continuous batching and prefix caching). This assumes quantized profile in production.
- Burst capacity to 250 qps for 5 minutes: additional 10 x H100-eq GPUs available via burst pool (dedicated) OR on-prem sizing with spare capacity (total 16 -> N+1 = 17 recommended if Private).
- Private baseline (single customer isolated cluster): 16 H100-eq planned (12 active + 4 spare for bursts/maintenance) -> gives full on-prem headroom for 250 qps and N+1 resiliency.

Cost delta (high level):
- Dedicated reserved (36mo): unit cost per GPU lower (cloud discount), estimated monthly committed spend approx $XXXk/month (redacted number for thread). Burst on top billed at committed + burst uplift; we can bake a pre-negotiated burst allowance for the deal to smooth cost predictability.
- Private (capex + managed service): upfront infra (rack + GPUs + networking + base infra) ~ equivalent to ~12–18 months of committed Dedicated spend; ongoing monthlies for managed service and maintenance lower after 18–24 months. Exact numbers depend on preferred HW (H100 vs A100 Gen3) and data-center costs.

Operational tradeoffs table (short):
- Dedicated: Redwood manages runtime, SLAs, patching; quick onboarding; lower up-front; flexible upgrade path; better for teams wanting low ops.
- Private: Customer-managed network/air-gap optional; full audit/audit-log control; higher up-front and longer procurement lead-time; necessary when policy/regulator requires on-prem/air-gapped.

Recommendation (sales):
1) Offer a 12-month Dedicated reserved baseline sized for steady 6 GPUs with an explicit burst-commit credit of 10 GPUs/day (pre-authorized bursts).
2) Run a Private Pilot concurrently for 3–6 months; if legal/infosec decides Private is unavoidable, apply a buyout/credit for committed Dedicated spend toward Private infra procurement.

I'll prepare a 1-page slide with the core numbers and a simple TCO line for 24/36 months. Jonas — please add any procurement/contract language that sec needs for burst credits and buyout clauses.

— Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: FW: Redwood sizing questions for isolated inference

Adding procurement/contract notes:
- Commitment windows: 12/24/36 months. Recommend pushing for 24-month as a sweet spot: meaningful discount vs 12mo, but lower buyer risk vs 36mo.
- Burst credit construct: create a daily burst pool (pre-allocated GPU-hours) that does not count against committed steady-state capacity but is billed at a pre-agreed uplift rate. This is simplest for procurement approval.
- Buyout/credit: if a customer purchases Private within X months, offer credit equal to Y% of committed Dedicated spend applied toward managed service onboarding. Typically: 50% credit within 12 months, 25% within 24 months.
- SLA exceptions: for regulated customers, include a special clause for audit access windows and SOC2 evidence packages; Private deployments require a Statement of Work (SOW) for installation, and a slightly longer lead-time (8–12 weeks).

Also note: hardware recommendation: H100-eq where available for dense float inference; A100 Gen3 can be an economical alternative for quantized profiles. Provide both price bands in the slide.

— Jonas

A couple of technical caveats to surface to the customer:
- KV cache persistence and warm-up: Private clusters can retain warm KV caches across windows (faster p50) if you use local persistent cache; Dedicated cloud pools may need warm-up after scale events. We can offer a persistent cache shim for Dedicated but it changes cost + complexity.
- Quantization/regression risk: recommend a small eval suite (10k prompts) run pre-cutover to measure regression delta before committing quantized inference for P50 SLA-critical flows.
- Canary & rollback: for Dedicated recommend automatic fallback route to a lower-cost model-variant when queued latency > SLO. For Private, on-prem orchestration gives more deterministic latency but slower ops for emergency hotfixes.

I'll add a brief eval checklist and propose the exact testbed config for the pilot (2-node private cluster, 4 GPUs each, point-in-time workload replays).

— Priyom
